I will not say which airline I work for, but being a minority in the minority of a work force has provided me with a unique job experience.
I am a straight male flight attendant. AMA!
How much of a problem is jet lag for you?

I have enough seniority to hold a schedule that brings me home Almost every night. However when flight attendants travel the long routes your inquiring about they get extra rest at the end of the trip.

There are a lot of federal regulations pertaining to crew rest for any situation you can think of, and then most flight attendants are unionized and have contracts that provide even more rules about rest.

How do you guys/girls always look so "fresh". I have been on some long haul flights and it has always baffled me when I wake up during a flight how you lot always seem like eermmm as fresh as a daisy.

That's top secret.

But really it's just something you learn from doing the job, tips and tricks that have been developed by generations of flight attendants. During the 60-70s the regulations for working hours and rest were much looser so flight attendants really had to figure out how to stay fresh.

Typically flight attendants always have at least an overnight bag packed even if we are scheduled to be home that night, just in case we do get stuck. So we have our toothbrushes, mouthwash, deodorant, hairspray, change of socks/ nylons, etc.

Straight male flight attendant. Packs nylons. Hmmm.

J/k A good paying job is a good paying job.

Can you guys just try not to bump me everytime you walk down the aisle?
I actually don't pack hairspray either, just listing ways flight attendants stay fresh.

Bumping in the aisles is a sticky situation. Flight attendant size, passenger size, the passenger nests to the passenger size all are involved. Then it depends if the flight attendant or passenger even try to avoid it. A lot of passengers don't even try to lean in slightly when they see me coming with a 500lb cart, they gunna get bumped.
Do crews stay together? Pilots and flight attendants? Or do you get mixed up for every flight?
Depends on the airline and the type of trip. If it's a turn (domestic there and back) they'll typically stay together. The flight attendants generally stick together if they do switch planes.
How much do alcoholic beverages cost? Can I order like 6 drinks at once or is there a limit?

In coach between five and eight dollars (typically). Besides not having much room for 6 drinks in a tray table, they have to be opened to be served, no we can't load you up, we can come back and get you more but I would never leave six drinks with one person at once. Also don't want anyone giving the drinks they buy to other people (minors).
What if I wanted 2 cause the first one goes down fast?
I'll sometimes do two (tipping helps), but someone getting drunk on a plane is a big risk and if I'm the one responsible for getting you drunk, I can get in loads of trouble.
I was not aware that flight attendants were tipped. Luckily I've never been on a plane, so I haven't stiffed anyone.
It's entirely optional. Appreciated, but not missed.
As a passenger, what can we do that will make your job easier but will also make our trip easier/more comfortable/etc.?

Thank you for asking, you i gut regret it though ;)

1) keep your shoes on

2) keep your socks on

3) keep your feet on he floor/ seat if you're spread out. NOT IN THE AIR

4) don't argue with the flight attendants about bags. We know our planes, 99% of the time if we say a a bag won't fit, it won't fit. We don't care it fit on your last plane ride.

5) don't overstuff your bag, the dimensions for bags is online on the airlines site, they are for your bag when it's full, not empty.

6) don't make references to airplane crashes, and don't try and make jokes. For two weeks after German wings we had passengers as they got on ask the pilots if either of em needed a hug and if they felt ok. Very distasteful.

7) headphones, they're not expensive

8) if you have a baby, do not ask the flight attendant for milk or diapers, nor can we heat the milk you brought, no we won't change your baby.

9) don't yell at flight attendants, we get paid to enforce rules that we don't help create. We can't offer you flight vouchers or refunds, all that has to be done off the plane, and yelling at your flight attendant makes an unpleasant experience for the whole plane.

Now for things you can do that are positive.

1) check the airlines website for any fees, they're not as "hidden" as many people think. Spirit who is known for being the king of fees actually gives you them straight forward. If you book through a 3rd party site they' won't have any of this info, you have to go to the airlines website.

2) give yourself extra time, it sucks more to rush than to spend an hour sitting in an airport

3) don't make any time sensitive plans after your flight, you don't want to land and have a date or job interview two hours later, because if we are delayed your s.o.l. And don't tell us what you need to get home for, it's not going to grant the plane priority departure status.

4) read the inflight menu card, don't guess and check when ordering a drink.

More to come, gotta fly.
